meeting_header: Date: 2025-07-02 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Location: Zoom | Attendees: Jamie Lopez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Chen (Arcadia), Maya Patel (Arcadia), Liam O'Neill (Arcadia)
summary: Intro call to understand Arcadia's requirements for customer insights generation. Primary asks: long context (8k-16k), multilingual support for en/es/pt, tool-calling to fetch customer metadata, and option evaluation between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Security and compliance gating (KMS, audit logs, SSO) were raised. Agreed next steps include benchmarks, sample data ingestion, and pricing draft.
topics: Model choices (open models: Mistral, Mosaic, Llama variants; tradeoffs)
Tool-calling / external API hooks for customer metadata
Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
Security: KMS, audit logs, SSO, data retention
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jamie from Redwood, with priya our solutions engineer. quick intro?
[00:06] Evan (Arcadia): yeah hey i'm evan, head of data at arcadia, we do consumer insights from cross-channel conversations, good to meet you all.
[00:12] Maya (Arcadia): maya here, ml lead, focused on NLU and pipeline.
[00:16] Liam (Arcadia): liam - security. quick heads up we have strict compliance so will ask a few infra Qs.
[00:22] Priya (Redwood SE): great, thanks. goal today is to map your inference needs — model selection, context length, tool-calling, and options for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[00:30] Evan: our big pain is context. we have multi-turn customer histories, sometimes 6-8k tokens and occasionally more, plus embeddings for retrieval. so an 8k baseline, ideally 16k for some flows.
[00:40] Jamie: yep that's common. when you say 6-8k, is that mostly full conversation or extra metadata?
[00:44] Evan: mostly full conversation, plus metadata like product ids and session notes that we want the model to see for summarization and persona-aware replies.
[00:50] Priya: ok, there are two axes: model architecture and deployment. for model choices we typically recommend trying a high-quality open model with 16k context support — some mMistral and mosaicrev variants have options, also llama 3 derivatives. but the hardware/quantization tradeoffs matter.
[01:05] Maya: can you clarify "mMistral"?
[01:07] Priya: sorry, mis-said — i mean Mistral 7B and the 7B-instruct family, also Mistral-XL has longer context variants. mosaicml has mosaic-instruct-8k, but there are 8k vs 16k builds. names get messy across forks.
[01:19] Evan: are those supported on Hosted? and what's the latency/sec token like?
[01:24] Jamie: yes hosted supports many curated open models; we publish perf profiles. latency depends on context length, model size, and batching. for a 7B-class at 8k context on our standard hosted node you might see 80-120 ms per token under light load; on Dedicated with reserved GPUs we can optimize kernels and batching to push latency down and control throughput.
[01:40] Liam: ok from security, we need encryption at rest, KMS integration for keys, audit logs, and SSO with SAML. can Redwood Private be air-gapped?
[01:48] Priya: Private can be deployed in a VPC or on-prem with customer-managed networking. we support KMS/HSM integrations and detailed audit logs. air-gapped on-prem is possible but it is a more involved integration — we typically scope that as a separate project.
[02:00] Evan: tool-calling — we need the model to call internal product-metadata service to enrich responses, not expose raw PII. how does Redwood handle tool-calls?
[02:08] Priya: our runtime supports function/tool calling and structured outputs. typical pattern: the model returns a tool-call intent, our orchestration layer dispatches to a secure microservice, fetches data, and returns the structured payload to the model for finalization. with Dedicated or Private, the tool-caller can run inside your VPC so data never leaves your network if that's required.
[02:28] Maya: latency is my worry — if every call triggers an API to our internal services, that could add 100-200ms per turn. can we cache?
[02:34] Priya: yes — prefix caching and KV cache reduce repeated lookups. we also recommend batching calls and local caching for common identifiers. Redwood Optimize can suggest caching and batching rules based on traces.
[02:46] Evan: on model quality vs cost: we saw Anthropic and OpenAI beat open models on certain benchmarks. our budget is tight though. what's the right tradeoff?
[02:56] Jamie: good question — common pattern is hybrid routing: use a smaller open model for most queries and route high-risk or higher-quality needs to a larger model or external provider. Redwood supports smart routing by policy — latency, cost, or safety thresholds.
[03:10] Liam: about data retention — our legal team requires logs be retained for 1 year, but with restricted access. can Redwood do token-level redaction in logs?
[03:18] Priya: we support configurable retention and can redact PII in logs. in Private deployments you can enforce retention in your infra. Hosted has options for limited retention and stricter audit roles. we'll include details in the security pack.
[03:30] Maya: how tricky is it to run 16k context? we have some flows that need full session context + related tickets, pushing near 12-16k.
[03:38] Priya: two considerations: model support for 16k and memory/kv cache management. some 7B/13B models have 16k windows natively; for larger contexts we use sliding windows and KV cache. on Dedicated we can tune batch sizes and kernel selection — sometimes quantized execution plus fused attention kernels keep memory and latency acceptable.
[03:57] Evan: can you share an example perf profile?
[04:00] Jamie: yes — we'll share a spreadsheet with tokens/sec, ms/token at 8k and 16k for Mistral, Mosaic, and Llama-3 variants on both Hosted and Dedicated configurations.
[04:08] Maya: multilingual — we need en/es/pt support, do models degrade significantly?
[04:13] Priya: multilingual performance varies. some open models are strong in en/es but weaker in pt. we usually recommend evaluating on your  sample prompts. Redwood Console includes per-route quality tracking so we can surface regressions.
[04:26] Evan: awesome. i also want to understand cost math — tokens in vs out, embeddings for retrieval, store costs for retriever index.
[04:34] Jamie: pricing varies by model and deployment. Hosted is usage-based per token and embedding unit; Dedicated is commit-based with unit pricing for PO. embeddings and vector store are priced separately. Jamie: we'll draft sample cost for a 1M request-per-month baseline and one pilot with 50k monthly active users.
[04:50] Liam: any compliance docs you can share?
[04:52] Jamie: yes SOC 2, ISO summaries, and our security pack — we'll attach.
[04:56] Maya: one more — tool-calling security: we want the model to never see raw customer emails, only hashed ids. can Redwood orchestrate that?
[05:04] Priya: absolutely. tool-calling payloads can be transformed at the orchestration layer and we can enforce schema contracts so the model only receives allowed fields.
[05:14] Evan: ok let's talk pilot shape — i imagine a 4-week pilot: ingest 10k transcripts, run inference to produce unified summaries and NPS-like insights, measure latency and cost, and evaluate quality vs our current heuristics. thoughts?
[05:26] Priya: that sounds reasonable. for pilot infra we suggest Dedicated reserved pool for more predictable perf and the ability to do kernel tuning. Hosted can work for quick starts but Dedicated reduces variance for benchmarks.
[05:36] Maya: we may want to try Hosted first for ease then flip to Dedicated for the pilot. is migration painful?
[05:41] Jamie: it's designed to be seamless at the API layer — same endpoints and rollouts. data and models are pinned per deployment. we may need to coordinate model caches and quantization artifacts when moving to Dedicated, but it's a normal workflow.
[05:53] Evan: competitors — we benchmarked Cohere and saw decent latency but cost was high; OpenAI quality is good but we're concerned about data residency. Anthropic had a safety edge for some prompts.
[06:03] Priya: we can run head-to-head evals during the pilot if you share test prompts. our eval harness supports automated A/B quality metrics and can tie regressions to prompts in Console.
[06:14] Liam: for SSO, we need SAML2 and SCIM for provisioning. supported?
[06:18] Jamie: yes SAML and SCIM supported for Enterprise accounts. we'll include setup docs.
[06:22] Maya: any limits on function calls per minute? we're likely to have bursts.
[06:27] Priya: Dedicated allows configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. Hosted has rate limits per account but we can increase for pilots. we'll include recommended quotas based on your expected QPS.
[06:36] Evan: question on embeddings — we plan to build a retriever with 512-d embeddings, how does Redwood recommend storing vectors?
[06:41] Priya: we support connector patterns to vector DBs and also an optional managed vector store. retrieval latency and cost depend on index type (flat vs hnsw) and region. we can help with an architecture doc.
[06:53] Maya: ok tldr on choices: start Hosted to iterate, move to Dedicated for pilot if perf needed, consider Private only if legal requires on-prem.
[07:01] Jamie: correct. one more note — quantization: 4-bit QAT or PTQ can reduce memory and cost but sometimes impacts generation quality; we'll include recommended quant profiles per model and workload.
[07:14] Evan: perfect, let's lock down dates. we'll aim to have sample data up by next friday.
[07:18] Maya: yes i'll get the sanitized datasets uploaded.
[07:21] Liam: i'll review the security pack and follow up with questions.
[07:24] Jamie: great — recap of next steps: priya runs benchmarks, maya uploads data, and i send pricing and the security pack. we'll schedule a 30-min follow-up once benchmarks done.
[07:36] Evan: thanks everyone.
[07:38] Jamie: thanks, talk soon.

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-transcriptions (model names like "mMistral"), speaker overlaps, and filler words. timestamps are approximate and every ~30-90s.
